chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Abu Ayyub, from Sulayman ibn Khalid, who said:

I asked Abu 'Abd Allah عليه السلام about a man who struck his daughter while she was pregnant, and she miscarried her child. Then the woman's husband brought a claim against her father, so the woman said: If there is a diyah for this miscarried fetus, then my share of inheritance from it is a gift to my father.
He عليه السلام said: "What she has assigned to him from her share is valid for her father."
He عليه السلام said: "And her father must pay to her husband two-thirds of the diyah of the miscarried fetus."

key_terms.حَامِلٌ: pregnant; carrying a child in the womb
key_terms.دِيَةٌ: financial compensation due for unlawful bodily harm or death
key_terms.ضَرَبَ: struck physically, causing the injury in question
key_terms.فَطَرَحَتْ: she cast out; meaning she miscarried
key_terms.مِيرَاثِي: my inheritance share from the deceased fetus
key_terms.هِبَةٌ: a gift; voluntary transfer of one's share

ai.seo_question: If a father causes his pregnant daughter to miscarry, how is the diyah divided according to Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning diyah for a miscarried fetus caused by the mother's father striking her. It states that the woman may cede her inherited share of the diyah to her father, while the remaining two-thirds are to be paid by him to her husband. The report pertains to family law, liability, and inheritance shares in cases of wrongful harm.
